description: You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise. You must rotate the image in-place.
intuition: A 90-degree clockwise rotation can be decomposed into two simple operations: first transpose (flip along the main diagonal, swapping rows and columns), then reverse each row. Each operation is easy to implement in-place, and together they produce the desired rotation.
approach: Transpose and Reverse: First transpose the matrix (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]), then reverse each row. This achieves a 90-degree clockwise rotation in-place.
explanation:
1. Transpose the matrix: swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all i < j.
   - This flips the matrix along its main diagonal.
2. Reverse each row.
   - Combined with the transpose, this produces a 90-degree clockwise rotation.
3. The operation is done in-place with no extra matrix allocation.
hints: A 90-degree clockwise rotation = transpose + reverse each row.
A 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation = transpose + reverse each column.
You only need to swap elements above the diagonal during transpose.

phases.label: Swap entries above the diagonal with their transposes

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: The triangular transpose loop and the row reversals are separate passes over O(n²) entries.

complexityVariables.n: Number of rows and columns in the square matrix.
